da4ozp:800: From 0 to 1: Lenovo's resource intelligent inspection Agent innovation based on the Strands Agent SDK by awschina on 21 Nov 2025 in Industries Permalink Share Introduction The digitalization wave has already driven enterprises to migrate from traditional data centers to public cloud platforms, and now they are experiencing another huge technological transformation, standing on the wave of the shift from digitalization to intelligence. This shift is not just a technology upgrade, but a fundamental change in operations philosophy. The rapid development of AI has provided strong momentum for operations transformation, enabling us to achieve three key goals: shifting from passive fault response to proactive risk prediction; identifying potential risks in time through AI; and improving operations efficiency and accuracy. For frontline operations staff, this transformation is highly significant. They will be freed from repetitive work such as tedious daily inspections and routine maintenance, and instead focus on more creative and challenging tasks like system architecture optimization and performance tuning. This lets them fully leverage the professional experience accumulated over years, truly demonstrating their unique value in handling complex problems. Lenovo's challenges in operations inspection and the need for intelligent operations In Lenovo's public cloud operations team, monitoring service status and preventing potential issues is one of the key daily tasks for ensuring stable system operation. Traditional resource inspection methods rely on manual operations and have clear limitations. This approach is not only time-consuming and labor-intensive, but also prone to oversights, making it difficult to detect faults in a timely manner and, in severe cases, affecting business continuity. As cloud resource deployment scales up, manual inspection can no longer achieve full coverage. In addition, the public cloud operations team lacks project-level inspection reports as a reference, making it hard to assess the status of each project—making an intelligent solution urgent. The growing maturity of AI Agent technology and LLM capabilities provides a new way to solve these challenges. Lenovo's Innovation Center team needs to develop an intelligent multi-agent collaborative operations system to address daily inspection of a large number of resources, process complex business report generation needs based on private knowledge and best practices, and solve problems that humans cannot solve manually. Intelligent transformation is both a technology upgrade and a change in operations philosophy. This will ensure that Lenovo's public cloud operations team maintains efficient and reliable IT operations capabilities in an environment of continuously expanding cloud resources, and it was also the original intention behind developing the intelligent inspection assistant.
